title: Yuzvendra Chahal Says Rehab Followed Drinking That Crossed All Limits
excerpt: The India leg-spinner told Aakash Chopra's podcast that he spent 26 days in a rehabilitation centre after his divorce, and described the anxiety attacks that came with that period.
body:
• Yuzvendra Chahal says his drinking "crossed all limits" after his divorce and that he spent 26 days in a rehabilitation centre after his last county cricket season.
  • The India leg-spinner, the IPL's highest wicket-taker with 233 wickets, spoke on Aakash Chopra's Baith & Bol podcast; his divorce was finalised in March 2025.
  • He also described anxiety attacks with physical symptoms, and said he took a break from T20 cricket that year because his mindset was not right.
  • Chahal says he stopped drinking late last year and felt the effect in the last IPL: fitter in the gym and fielding drills, and emotionally steadier.

Yuzvendra Chahal has spoken publicly about the period in which alcohol took over his life after his divorce, saying he checked into a rehabilitation centre for 26 days after deciding the drinking had gone too far. The 36-year-old India leg-spinner made the remarks on Baith & Bol, a podcast hosted by former India opener Aakash Chopra, according to Livemint's report of the conversation.

What Chahal said

Asked what made him quit alcohol, Chahal said the turning point came after his last season of county cricket. He said he realised that continuing would damage the thing he loves most — cricket — and that the decision changed his personal life: his maturity increased, his emotions settled, and at the last IPL his body felt years younger in gym work, fielding drills and training.

"It crossed all limits, so I checked into a rehab centre and stayed there for 26 days."

— Yuzvendra Chahal, on the Baith & Bol podcast

Chahal traced the habit to his early IPL years, when he was young and partying was part of the circuit after he first joined the league in 2011. He recalled former South Africa batter AB de Villiers telling him that balance is key in life — advice he said sounds easy and is not. After his divorce, he said, things became excessive and his mental state was poor. Livemint reports he revealed in March this year that he had stopped drinking late last year.

Anxiety, scrutiny and a break from the game

The account goes beyond alcohol. Chahal described anxiety attacks with physical symptoms — a racing heartbeat and episodes in which he could not speak clearly — and said public commentary on his personal life weighed on him, CricTracker reports. He said he took a break from the game that year, played only two white-ball matches and skipped T20s because his mindset was not right. He credited his best friend and family for standing by him.

His marriage to social media influencer Dhanashree Verma ended with a divorce finalised in March 2025. Chahal, who plays for Punjab Kings and recently retired from first-class cricket, remains the IPL's highest wicket-taker with 233 wickets; he took 12 wickets in 14 matches in the 2026 IPL season and has 217 wickets across 72 ODIs and 80 T20Is for India.

Why the account matters

Elite cricketers rarely describe rehab in this level of detail, and Chahal's account is specific about the sequence that helped him: recognising the problem, entering a professional rehabilitation programme, and rebuilding through training. Readers who recognise the pattern he describes — drinking escalating after a personal crisis, anxiety with physical symptoms — should note that the step he took was professional help, arranged through a rehabilitation centre, backed by family support. He says he is now in a happier place, enjoying life away from the game as well as in it.
